english.title: Young person being employed on premises with gaming machines - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a young person aged **(..SPECIFY AGE..), who was employed to perform a function on premises where a Category A, B, C, or D gaming machine was situated, you were or may have been required in the course of that employment to perform a function, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FUNCTION..), in connection with a gaming machine
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 54(2) and 62(2)(b) of the Gambling Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a young person having been employed
to perform a function on premises
where a Category A, B, C or D gaming machine was situated
were/may have been required in the course of his employment
to perform a function in connection with a gaming machine

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 45 of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that "young person" means an individual aged 16 or 17.

other.penalty:
Fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months
